external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: A duty engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app opened by duty engineers in a browser.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer.
processes.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
processes.notes: The API is served cross-origin to the console. CORS origins and credential handling were not recorded.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A scheduled importer that pulls, parses, archives, and posts planned work orders.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: It presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or the session that created it. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve app
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin. Allowed origins and credential handling were not recorded.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: It was not recorded whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer, or how the importer identifies the partner.

data_flows.name: write archive
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate and authority to move a crew or change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: An account there can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day; a corporate laptop holds none of those rights.

trust_boundaries.description: A zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's data classification is confidential because it holds crew names, crew mobile numbers, and tokens or sessions associated with job orders.
assumptions.basis: The stated database contents include personal contact information and credentials or session data.
